0434a411803905bad418971f437d75694530be03.summary: SentinelOne report on FIN7, a financially motivated group with Russian origins active since 2012. It covers AvNeutralizer, an EDR-impairment tool sold on underground forums and used by several ransomware groups, and a new variant that causes denial of service in protected processes. Also covered: Powertrash loaders delivering Diceloader and Core Impact implants, an SSH-based persistence backdoor, and automated SQL injection attacks. Pseudonym attributions are stated with confidence levels.

hedges: Advertisements by goodsoft, lefroggy, killerAV and Stupor are assessed with high confidence as belonging to the FIN7 cluster; the actors likely use multiple pseudonyms.
Report hypothesises that AvNeutralizer was likely sold on criminal forums, with Black Basta among early buyers; a FIN7-Black Basta link is only a hypothesis.
Stupor's AvNeutralizer version is attributed to the same individual with high confidence.
Whether FIN7 executed intrusions using the LockBit locker with AvNeutralizer cannot be conclusively determined; no direct evidence links them.
One Core Impact RSA key is attributed to FIN7 with medium confidence; overlapping loader configurations make this uncertain.
Checkmarks ProxyShell and automated SQL injection intrusions are attributed to FIN7 and the Auto-SQLi module with medium confidence.
Suspected espionage intention behind the SSH-based backdoor install is a suspicion, not a confirmed finding.
The group's use of multiple pseudonyms and collaboration with other criminal entities is said to make attribution more challenging.
